Planning doc · Aug 2026

Basement Renovation Plan

A gym with a built-in desk nook, a small 3-piece bathroom, and a compact laundry in one long narrow basement. Three price levels below — same look at each, more of it as the number goes up. All sizes and prices are estimates until the space is measured.

SHEET 01

Floor plan

SCALE ~1/4" · DIMS UNVERIFIED

The wet stuff clusters at the entry end, where the plumbing already is: the small laundry and a new 3-piece bathroom sit side by side (about 6' each across the width), sharing walls and drains. Everything past the partition is one continuous gym — with a built-in desk nook along the wall just inside the door, so there's a real workstation without giving up a room. The half-built partition stays, gets finished, and now carries both the entry door and the bathroom door.

36' (planning)8'28'
40'8'32'

Why the bathroom goes there

It shares the laundry's wet wall and the existing drain stack — shortest pipe runs, one wet zone, one door off the entry landing. The open question is below the slab: if the sewer line sits higher than the new drains, the bathroom needs a sewage ejector pump (a sealed pit + pump, ~$2–4K extra). Finding the stack, cleanout, and sewer depth is now the top item on the measuring trip.

SHEET 02

What's down there now

FROM PHOTOS · AUG 2026

Good bones, honestly: dry-looking gray block, open joists, a black rack already doing the aesthetic's heavy lifting, laundry machines on the plumbing wall, and a half-built partition that just needs mud, paint, and a door. The middle zone is storage — fridges, coolers, and pantry racks all leave for the garage before anything else happens.

Keeping

  • Power rack + rings, bar, plates, bench, heavy bag — the gym seed
  • Folding treadmill — parks against the long wall
  • Washer + dryer and the laundry plumbing wall as-is
  • The new partition — gets finished, insulated, painted, doored
  • Block walls + open ceiling — the look, not a problem to hide

Unknowns that shape the plan

  • True dimensions — 30–40' long, 10–15' wide; everything here scales
  • Headroom — joist height, and the duct that dips at the laundry end
  • Moisture — 48-hour plastic test decides paint type and flooring prep
  • Panel capacity + furnace/water-heater location — not in the photos
  • Windows? — none visible; one would reshuffle the plan
  • Sewer depth + stack location — decides whether the bathroom drains by gravity or needs an ejector pump

Rule for every tier: nothing gets painted, glued, or framed until the moisture test passes and the tape measure has been down there. That trip is Sheet 08.

SHEET 03

The three price levels

MOCKUPS · GYM ELEVATION + VIGNETTES

Same palette and layout at every price. Each tier is designed to stack on the one below it — Tier 1's paint and rubber are still there if Tier 2's trades show up next year.

The look comes straight from your three reference photos: dark warm walls, black steel, brass, oak, and warm built-in lighting — the glowing line where wall meets ceiling, mirrors lit from behind. Every level opens with your actual room, edited to that level by an image model (FLUX, running free on your own Cloudflare account) — same walls, same rack, same machines. The bathroom and desk nook are concept renders, since those corners don't exist yet.

TIER 1

Budget build

$3.5K–6.5K · 2–4 WEEKENDS · DIY

Dark paint on the gym walls, warm white everywhere else, rubber floor, an LED strip light where the wall meets the ceiling, real light fixtures instead of bare bulbs, and the desk nook made intentional with a wall panel, sconce, and rug. Done in a few weekends. (The bathroom is inherently Tier 2+ work — plumbing and permits.)

What happens

SHEET 06

Cost comparison

US 2026 RANGES · NOT QUOTES

What actually moves the number: the bathroom's below-slab plumbing (a needed ejector pump swings it $2–4K), who hangs the drywall, and ceiling treatment (black-out spray is ~10× cheaper than drywall overhead).

Do it in stages if you want: Tier 1 this fall for under $7K, live in it, then add Tier 2 pieces one at a time — nothing from Tier 1 gets ripped out.

SHEET 07

Keep the block, or finish it?

THE STANDING QUESTION

It's cinder block (CMU), not brick — and painted dark, it looks right for this. The answer at every level: paint the block in the gym, and only spend on framing where a room needs to feel soft and warm — the office at Tier 2, everything at Tier 3.

OptionCost (~770 sq ft walls)You getWatch out
Paint it$400–800 DIYHonest industrial; coursing shows; reversibleMoisture test first — damp block wants breathable mineral paint or limewash, never a sealing film
Skim / parge, then limewash$1–2/sq ft DIY · $3–6 proSoft, monolithic, "old European gym" look — good middle optionLabor-heavy; still wants breathable finish
Fur + insulate + drywall$7–12/sq ft installedFully finished, warm, hides wiringLoses 3–5" per side of a narrow room; moisture detailing must be right

Before any of them: the 48-hour plastic-sheet moisture test, and a walk around the outside (gutters, downspouts, grade). $0–300 of exterior fixes beats $3K of interior regret. If the test comes back wet, that's a stop-and-reassess — not a paint-over.

SHEET 08

Next steps

PHASE 0 · ~2 HRS + 48H WAITS · ~$50

The measuring trip

  1. Tape measure: true length + width, slab-to-joist, slab-to-lowest-duct (both ends)
  2. Find + photograph: panel (cover open), furnace, water heater, behind the white door, any windows, any floor drain
  3. Moisture test: plastic squares taped to wall ×2 + slab ×1, read at 48h
  4. Find the sewer: main stack, cleanout, and how deep the sewer line runs — gravity drain vs ejector pump for the bathroom
  5. Radon kit in the gym end (people will live down here now)
  6. Scratch-test the tan floor in a corner — paint or overlay?

Decisions on the table

  1. Tier — 1, 2, 3, or "1 now, wired for 2"
  2. Walls — paint / skim+limewash / frame (rec: paint the gym, frame the office at T2+)
  3. Layout — A, unless a window turns up (then B)
  4. Bathroom timing — build it fully at Tier 2, or rough-in the plumbing now and finish at Tier 3

Measurements come back → the plan and these mockups get re-scaled to reality, and the chosen tier gets a real shopping list.

Assumptions: 36'×12' planning basis (real range 30–40 × 10–15, unverified) · ~7' to joists · moisture test passes · fridges + pantry move to the garage first.
